phases.name: Phase 0 · Positioning
phases.goal: Make the profile read as engineering, pick the flagship, measure the baseline.

tasks.text: Rewrite headline and resume around one story: production LLM systems, measured. Drop the six-role wishlist.
Resume top third: KaatDo (uptime, cancel latency, broker failure handling, users) and Ahead (sources, dedup rate, brief quality metric).
Benchmarking job bullets: how many models, which metrics you designed, which decisions changed because of your evals.
Cut the toolkit to what survives a ten-minute deep dive; everything else off or marked familiar.
Write the one-page design doc for the flagship project (India-domain eval suite).
Do two 60-minute timed practical problems cold, recorded; note where you stall.
Start the 4+ active GitHub days per week habit.

phases.name: Phase 1 · Fundamentals and signal
phases.goal: Coding fluency, written designs, the four reference implementations, flagship v1, first merged PRs.

tasks.text: 3 timed practical coding sessions per week (Practice page), Python first, TypeScript second.
1 written LLM-infra design per week, 45 minutes, then a 20-minute self-critique.
Reference implementation 1: tool-calling agent loop with structured outputs, retries, token/cost budget and a trace viewer, on both Claude and OpenAI APIs.
Reference implementation 2: an MCP server over something real (KaatDo broker abstraction or Ahead source registry) plus a client.
Reference implementation 3: eval harness with 200+ cases, three grader types, bootstrap confidence intervals, a regression gate.
Reference implementation 4: prompt-caching and batch cost study on Ahead's daily brief.
Flagship v1 live by 31 Jan with a public write-up.
Two merged PRs (docs, tests, small fixes) in a lab-adjacent repo.
One values primary source per week with half a page of your own notes, disagreements included.
Use Claude Code seriously for a week on a real project; write down where the harness helped and where it fell over.

phases.name: Phase 2 · Depth, network, first applications
phases.goal: Mock loops, flagship v2 with published evals, five informational conversations, first applications.

tasks.text: Two full mock loops per month (coding, design, customer conversation, values), recorded and reviewed.
Flagship v2: evals published with methodology, costs and failure analysis; the artifact linked in every application.
Five informational conversations with ICs at Anthropic / OpenAI India; share flagship findings, no asks in the first conversation.
Apply to Tier 1 roles once flagship v2 is live; one lab first, the other 3–4 weeks later.
Five merged PRs total, at least one non-trivial (a feature or a real bug with a test).
Write the 'Why Anthropic' and 'Why OpenAI' answers yourself; refine with Claude afterwards, per Anthropic's policy.
Two self-timed 4-hour builds, no AI, README written in the last 20 minutes.

phases.name: Phase 3 · Loops and iteration
phases.goal: Run the loops, post-mortem each round the same day, keep shipping monthly.

tasks.text: Complete at least two real loops.
Write a post-mortem the same day after every rejected round; adjust the practice mix.
One flagship release and one write-up per month.
1 Sep 2027 decision checkpoint: offer, re-apply window, or stepping-stone move.

phases.name: Stretch · Research engineering path (2028+)
phases.goal: Public research-engineering evidence, then Research Engineer applications with relocation.

tasks.text: Reproduce one alignment or eval paper end to end at small scale; publish code and results.
Sustained infrastructure contributions to Inspect or lm-evaluation-harness.
Apply to Research Engineer roles with a body of public work.

pillars.name: Practical coding
pillars.plan: Rotate the twelve shapes as 4-stage problems under a 60–90 minute timer, Python, tests included. Once a week do a fix-the-broken-codebase or refactor-this-file format.

pillars.name: System design
pillars.plan: Alternate LLM-infra prompts with enterprise-deployment prompts; one-page design, then defend it in a mock.

pillars.name: LLM implementation
pillars.plan: Build the four reference implementations on both APIs; know the docs cold; one week of serious Claude Code use.

pillars.name: Evaluation
pillars.plan: Eval-driven development on the flagship: golden set, rubric graders, LLM judge calibrated against human labels, regression gate, confidence intervals.

pillars.name: ML fundamentals
pillars.plan: The Amazon breadth list plus the DeepMind quiz is the union of what Google, Microsoft and Amazon ask. Flashcard it; derive, don't recite.

pillars.name: LLM internals
pillars.plan: Zero to Hero end to end, then attention from scratch in PyTorch, then the inference arithmetic.

pillars.name: Values and safety
pillars.plan: Read the primary sources and write your position in plain language, including disagreements, for both labs.

pillars.name: Behavioral and customer
pillars.plan: 8–10 quantified STAR stories mapped to Amazon LPs and Microsoft competencies; six recorded discovery-call mocks; two project deep dives (KaatDo, Ahead) with diagrams.

flagship.name: A. India-domain LLM evaluation suite (primary)
flagship.text: An open-source eval harness for Indian-language and India-domain tasks (Hindi, Bhojpuri, Telugu; agriculture, law, healthcare workflows you know from the clinic apps). Run Claude, GPT and open models; publish a leaderboard with methodology, confidence intervals, cost per task and failure analysis; build on Inspect so others can run it. Converts your benchmarking day job into public evidence and lines up with Anthropic's India eval work.

flagship.name: B. Production agent with MCP, evals and observability
flagship.text: Turn a piece of KaatDo or Ahead into an agent with an MCP server, tracing, cost controls, eval-gated releases and a written incident post-mortem. The FDE/Applied AI portfolio piece: a customer-shaped system, not a demo.

flagship.name: C. Finish Hoshlab
flagship.text: Write it up as a case study with measured outcomes: drafts accepted vs rejected, QA catch rate, cost per post. Finishing things is itself a signal.
